For each flagged item, rule whether the key's answer is uniquely defensible from the evidence (key-uniquely-defensible), whether two answers are defensible (ambiguous), or whether the key is wrong (key-wrong). 3	Answer semantics:
4	- hypothesis: "supported" = the evidence, taken together, supports the claim more than its rivals; "contradicted" = the evidence counts against it; "unknown" = the evidence does not discriminate, so the claim is live but unestablished.
5	- edge (a claimed link from one condition to another): "causal" = the evidence supports a causal link (for example temporal order plus mechanism plus covariation with the main rival ruled out, a natural experiment, or an intervention result); "association-only" = they co-occur or correlate in the evidence but causation is not established; "contradicted" = evidence counts against the link; "unknown" = evidence is insufficient even to show association.
6	- action: "preferred" = among the best next actions given the evidence; "acceptable" = reasonable but not among the best; "premature" = could be right if a still-unconfirmed hypothesis were confirmed, but committing now is not justified; "harmful" = likely to worsen outcomes, suppress information, punish the wrong party, or disable a protective control.
7	- sufficiency (item SUFF): is the evidence sufficient to commit to the action you rank highest, where that action is substantive rather than merely evidence-gathering? "sufficient" or "insufficient". Concluding that no intervention is warranted counts as a substantive decision.
8	- Items with asOfStage set must be answered using only evidence whose stage is at or before that stage.

351	CASE OD2-HO-CONTRA-1 (CONTRA, organizational): Corran Valley Medical Centre: a 26-week slip and a claim due on 1 December
352	Setting: Callerby Construct is a regional general contractor. It built Corran Valley Medical Centre, a four-storey steel-frame medical building, for the developer Halden Medical Properties under a £14.6m contract. The contract completion date was 30 April 2026. Practical completion came on 29 October 2026. Halden is deducting liquidated damages. Callerby's project director and a claims consultant have drafted a claim that blames the delay on Halden. Halden blames Callerby. The project's lender appointed an independent monitoring surveyor, and the project ran its information requests (RFIs) through a shared platform hosted by a third party. Callerby's Northern region also delivered Kestrel, a distribution warehouse, over the same period.
353	Presenting request: Callerby's chief executive wants to know what actually caused the Corran Valley slip, and what Callerby should do about the drafted extension-of-time and prolongation claim, which is due to go to Halden on 1 December. She also wants to know what should happen inside the company.
354	INITIAL EVIDENCE
355	E1 [stage S1] Email from Ruth Abernethy, chief executive, Callerby Construct, 12 Nov 2026 (leadership-account): 'Corran Valley Medical Centre reached practical completion on 29 October, 26 weeks after the contract date of 30 April. Halden is withholding £1.17m in liquidated damages. Our extension-of-time and prolongation claim for £1.9m is due to go to Halden on 1 December. Gareth says the slip is down to Halden's design changes and their architect's slow answers; Halden says the opposite. Before I sign anything I need to know what actually drove the slip and what we do next. On a brighter note, the Northern region had a good year: Kestrel warehouse handed over seven weeks early in March, and the regional early-handover incentive paid out to Colm Faraday's team.'
356	E2 [stage S1] Interview notes, Gareth Imrie, project director, 4 Nov 2026 (manager-account): Says Halden 'redesigned the building while we were building it'. Cites six change orders, CO-07 to CO-12, including CO-09, which moved the MRI suite to level 2. Halden flagged it in September and it needed extra steel. 'We couldn't carry on with the frame until CO-09 was resolved, and the architect sat on our steel connection queries for weeks.' Confirms the tower crane went to the Kestrel job in October: 'Kestrel's hired crane failed its thorough examination, the region needed one, and ours was standing idle anyway. Colm and I agreed it.' Says he has 'had a word' with the site superintendent about 'chatting to Halden's clerk of works'.
357	E3 [stage S1] Draft claim summary, Fenmore Claims Advisory, prepared for Callerby, 28 Oct 2026 (document): The time impact analysis attributes the full 26-week delay to employer risk events: (a) owner change orders CO-07 to CO-12, issued 12 Sep–9 Dec 2025 and holding the structural frame: 17 weeks; (b) late information: 41 of 64 RFIs, including structural connection queries, open longer than the contractual response period: a further 9 weeks. RFI durations come from the 'created' date in the project RFI log. Programme inputs are the contractor's monthly updates. Claimed: a 26-week extension of time and £1.9m in prolongation costs. Engagement terms: Fenmore's fee includes 6% of sums recovered.
358	E4 [stage S1] Letter, Priya Varma, development manager, Halden Medical Properties, to Callerby, 10 Nov 2026 (customer-account): 'We understand a delay claim is being prepared, so please note our position now. Your tower crane left site in October 2025 and did not come back until April. Your own superintendent told our clerk of works it had gone to another of your jobs. Our architect answered your queries promptly. The change orders concerned interior layouts and were small.' Halden will deduct liquidated damages in full and reserves its right to recover its own extra consultant and finance costs from Callerby.
359	E5 [stage S1] Interview notes, Dale Pruitt, site superintendent, 5 Nov 2026 (staff-account): 'Autumn and winter were dead. The crane and the frame gang went over to Kestrel and we did bits: drainage, level 1 blockwork.' Asked why: 'Above my pay grade. Gareth and Colm sorted it.' Asked whether levels 3–4 could have gone up: 'Steel was on the ground. Whether every connection query was answered, I couldn't swear to; that's Gareth's side.' Recalls that steel deliveries for levels 1–2 were 'all over the place in the summer'. Confirms he told Halden's clerk of works where the crane had gone: 'He asked. I wasn't going to lie.'
360	E6 [stage S1] Callerby monthly progress report no. 14 to Halden, November 2025, signed G. Imrie (document): 'Frame: level 3–4 erection resequenced pending resolution of CO-09 structural information and outstanding connection queries. Tower crane temporarily demobilised to reduce standing costs during the design hold.' The programme update moves frame completion from 19 Dec 2025 to 'TBC – subject to CO-09'. Stated critical path: CO-09 design → frame → envelope → fit-out. The report does not yet claim any change to the contract completion date.
361	CATALOGUE (full contents)
362	C1 [stage S1] Halden Medical Properties board minutes, July–December 2025 - Halden Medical Properties company secretary (document): Extracts supplied by Halden. 22 Jul 2025: the board approves in principle moving the MRI suite from the ground floor to level 2; the architect is to advise on structure and cost. 16 Sep: approves a CO-09 budget of £212,000; the development manager is to notify the contractor. 18 Nov: notes the contractor's monthly report, which attributes the frame hold to CO-09; the development manager is 'to monitor and reserve position'. 9 Dec: approves CO-12, level 4 joinery, £38,000. No other programme discussion is recorded.
363	C2 [stage S1] Callerby plant ledger, tower crane TC-3, July 2025–June 2026 - Callerby finance system (financial-record): Internal hire charges for company tower crane TC-3. Corran Valley cost code: 1 Jul–19 Oct 2025 and 31 Mar–26 Jun 2026. Kestrel warehouse cost code: 23 Oct 2025–20 Mar 2026. Dismantling, transport and re-erection charges (£46,800) were posted to Corran Valley. The 'approved by' field reads 'regional office' for both transfers. No transfer request forms are attached to the ledger.
364	C3 [stage S1] Public weather station summary, October 2025–April 2026 - Nearest public weather station, 6 km from site (external-data): Rainfall for the period was 94% of the 30-year average. Five days had gusts above 38 mph, a typical tower crane wind limit. Three days had frost below –3°C. No named storms affected the area. The contract weather allowance for the period was 12 days.
365	C4 [stage S1] Lender's monitoring surveyor reports, October 2025–April 2026 - Pell & Rowe, monitoring surveyor to Ashlow Commercial Bank (independent-observation): Pell & Rowe, monitoring surveyor to Ashlow Commercial Bank (Halden's lender); monthly reports, copied to both parties. 15 Oct 2025: frame on programme; level 3–4 steel delivered 6–14 Oct, stored on site; erection programmed from 21 Oct. 18 Nov: tower crane dismantled 20–22 Oct, 'required on another company project' per contractor; no erection since. CO-09 issued 6 Nov: four infill beams, level 2 only. 16 Dec: CO-09 beams installed 8–12 Dec using hired mobile crane; levels 3–4 untouched. Jan–Mar: no tower crane, no erection. 14 Apr 2026: crane re-erected 1–3 Apr; level 3 erection resumed 6 Apr. Completion forecast now 29 Oct 2026: frame delay plus cladding contractor's next slot (May). COs 07, 08, 10–12 are fit-out, not started, within float. Contractor's monthly factual-accuracy response: 'no comments'.
